title: The Responsive W / Annotated chart
slide_intent: Separate fixed anchors from variable dimensions because controlled flexibility needs enough stability to remain identifiable.
strategic_value: The chart can help multiple Whitney designers vary the mark without losing its name placement and construction logic.
demonstration: A photographed chart combines a matrix of W variants, blue annotations and enlarged construction and word-placement examples.
practical_value: Use the chart to distinguish shape variation from construction and placement guidance; inspect the original before relying on small printed measurements.

content_islands.name: Variation matrix
content_islands.spec: Arrange increasingly deep and wide W variants across the left and lower chart.

content_islands.name: Construction notes
content_islands.spec: Group enlarged blue line, word and placement examples across the top and right.

content_islands.name: Identification
content_islands.spec: Retain the bold chart title at lower left and studio/date credit at lower right.

reference_purposes.Intent: The adjacent essay explains that a fixed element is needed to make the flexibility perceptible.
reference_purposes.Application: The chart supplies a matrix of possible forms and annotated construction examples.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying essay states that Whitney remains locked to the upper-left corner of the sign; it describes this as the fixed element within the flexible system.

ingredient.name: Fixed Whitney anchor, variable W
ingredient.role: Preserve a point of recognition while shape and dimensions vary.
ingredient.application: Keep Whitney at the upper-left corner of the sign while adapting the W to its available space.
ingredient.scope: Historical chart and accompanying essay. Small printed chart measurements should be checked in the source; the matrix is not an exhaustive set.
